messages.author: 05f098102a2ea7f2
messages.subject: lm, glm, gam, loess, rlm
parts:
Is there a ggplot2 resource that summarizes all the stat_smooth methods and describes their best case scenarios?
I'm thinking of a table or grid with key attributes that would help you quickly decide on use.

Thank you,
KD

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: lm, glm, gam, loess, rlm
parts:
No, because you can use any modelling function that follows the R
standard (i.e. data + modelling formula, and implements predict).
(standard errors are a bit harder because there's not a consistent
standard)

Hadley

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: lm, glm, gam, loess, rlm
parts:
And a couple of other points, just to clarify:

(i) the model formula has y for the response and x for the covariate,
no matter what the name of x and y in the data and the
ggplot()/qplot() call;
(ii) the RHS of the model formula is a function of x.

Dennis
